sources.title: auto-advance.md (context-shards)
sources.note: Whole file read. The only shard in the folder I was given; it is a design note for the auto-advance engine, not a loading-mechanism spec.

sources.title: explanation/workflow-phases.md
sources.note: Raw markdown, read whole. Docs page, unsigned.

sources.title: tutorials/first-session.md
sources.note: Read whole. Little of interest to the harness.

sources.title: package.json (humanlayer monorepo)
sources.note: Read whole. The silent runner scripts/run-silent.ts, scripts/hook-prepush.ts and scripts/hooks/pre-push are NOT in my file list, so their contents are unread.

sources.title: release-notes.md
sources.note: Keyword-scanned only (shard, orchestrate, verif, compact, fork, effort, backpressure, silent, hook) with surrounding lines, not read in full. Cards use the version headers.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: bun run scripts/run-silent.ts 'quality passed' bash -c 'oxlint --quiet apps packages contracts && bun run format'
cards.claim: The quality gate (lint plus format check) runs under a silent runner that prints a single success string and only shows output on failure, with oxlint in --quiet mode.
cards.evidence_detail: A config line in the repo. No measurement of context saved is given in these files. The runner's source is not in my bundle.
cards.landing: Wrap FixFlow's npm test/lint/mypy/pytest commands in a silent runner (ruff, mypy, pytest, jest, alembic check) and name the wrapper in CLAUDE.md. The backpressure post is the inventory's source for this idea.

cards.source_title: package.json: test and typecheck use the silent runner
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: bun run scripts/run-silent.ts 'tests passed' bun run test:local
cards.claim: Test and typecheck commands are each wrapped in the same silent runner with a one-phrase success message ('tests passed', 'typecheck passed'), so every verification command an agent runs has the same quiet-on-success contract.
cards.evidence_detail: Three scripts share the runner: quality, test, typecheck.
cards.landing: Give every verifier command in the phase routine one wrapper and one success string. A reviewer can then grep for that string in the PR body as a cheap check that the command was run.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "hook:quality": "bun run quality"
cards.claim: The hook scripts are thin aliases onto the same quality/typecheck commands (hook:quality is just 'bun run quality'; hook:typecheck is 'turbo run typecheck'), so a hook and a human run the identical command with no separate hook logic.
cards.evidence_detail: The settings file that binds these names to Claude Code hook events is not in my bundle, so what triggers them is unread.
cards.landing: If hooks are ever re-opened, bind them to the commands CI already runs so there is one definition of 'quality'. The hook-to-event wiring (settings.json) still needs to be found. Re-opens the skipped hooks decision.
cards.inventory_ref: A4 (humanlayer repo, listed without its scripts)

cards.source_title: package.json: hook:prepush with a blocking react-doctor scope
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: bun scripts/hook-prepush.ts && bunx react-doctor apps/riptide-ui --scope changed --blocking warning
cards.claim: The pre-push hook runs a custom prepush script and then a React-specific static checker scoped to changed files only, with warnings treated as blocking.
cards.evidence_detail: Config only; hook-prepush.ts content unread.
cards.landing: A changed-files-only check keeps the gate fast. A pre-push (not pre-commit) gate is a lighter version of the skipped pre-commit gate. Mark: re-opens the skipped pre-commit gate.

cards.source_title: package.json: githooks installs into the git common dir
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: cp scripts/hooks/pre-push $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks/pre-push
cards.claim: The hook installer copies a versioned pre-push script into the shared git common dir, so every worktree of the clone gets the same hook (the project runs a worktree per task).
cards.evidence_detail: One-line installer script.
cards.landing: FixFlow works in git worktrees (this session is one). Installing a hook into the common dir covers all of them. Re-opens the skipped hooks decision.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: bun run typecheck && bun run quality && bun run check:sentry-closures && bun run check:zod
cards.claim: One 'check' command chains typecheck, quality and two repo-specific invariant scripts (a Sentry closure check and a zod version check), so project-specific traps are mechanised in the same gate.
cards.evidence_detail: Config only; the two check scripts are unread.
cards.landing: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md lists traps in prose (empty EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN in eas.json, Sentry plugin in app.json, deploy from backend/). Turning each into a small script under one 'check' command moves rules out of CLAUDE.md. This bears directly on the 390-line trim.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: tools/oxlint/anti-slop/rules/max-ternary-depth.test.ts
cards.claim: The repo ships its own oxlint 'anti-slop' rules (max-ternary-depth, no-chained-type-assertions, no-conditional-spread, no-known-value-widening, no-object-parameters, no-widen-then-assert, no-unknown-type-aliases, and others) with a dedicated test script, turning agent bad habits into lint failures.
cards.evidence_detail: Names of ten rule test files visible in the script; rule contents unread.
cards.landing: Recurring FixFlow defect shapes (bare catch that hides offline, load-mutate-flush) could be ruff/ESLint custom rules instead of CLAUDE.md prose. Ties to his 'slop' framing.

cards.source_title: CONTRIBUTING.md: vouch gate requires a design discussion
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: run `/rpi:create-design-discussion` with the problem and the change you want to make.
cards.claim: Outside contributors must produce a finished design-discussion document (resolved questions with rejected options) before a maintainer will vouch for them, so review effort is spent on the plan before any code exists.
cards.evidence_detail: A policy statement, with a bot closing PRs from non-vouched authors.
cards.landing: Supports the 'review the plan not the PR' phase routine. FixFlow's 'Plan @ <sha>' PR body plus decisions journal is the same idea; the design document with 'Resolved Design Questions' and rejected options is a possible template for the journal.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: CI runs on every pull request, forks included, with no secrets. No test may need a real API key.
cards.claim: CI runs without secrets on every PR, and the rule that no test may need a real key makes the gate reproducible by any agent in any worktree.
cards.evidence_detail: Policy line.
cards.landing: FixFlow's pytest integration tests need FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL. A rule that agent-runnable checks need no secrets would keep the cold-resume trial (P1) from depending on credentials.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Keep each one to one change, with tests for new behavior.
cards.claim: Style rules for agent-written output are delegated to a skill file (.claude/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md) rather than written into the always-loaded instructions, and DB migrations are generated by tooling, never hand-written.
cards.evidence_detail: Two rules in the PR section.
cards.landing: Move topical rules (UI copy, migration conventions) from CLAUDE.md into skills under .claude/skills/ that are named from one line. FixFlow already has the skill-directory slot.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: You MUST NOT specify the 'model' unless the user explicitly asks you to.
cards.claim: HumanLayer injects a rule into every Claude Code session forbidding the parent from launching sub-agents in the background, from using run_in_background or resume, and from overriding the sub-agent model, so model routing is decided by configuration and not by the agent.
cards.evidence_detail: Verbatim system prompt text; the page calls obeying it 'CRITICAL' for the Agent tool to perform properly.
cards.landing: If FixFlow wants effort/model routing to be real, the routing table must live in agent files and the agent must be told not to pass its own model. Today any session can pick a model per call.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: No RPI sub-agent uses a fixed Opus model.
cards.claim: In Claude Code, the research sub-agents (codebase-analyzer, codebase-locator, codebase-pattern-finder) are Sonnet (or Haiku behind an experiment switch), web-search-researcher, implementer-agent and implementation-reviewer are Sonnet, and only outline-implementer-agent inherits the parent model.
cards.evidence_detail: Table of seven agents and their model aliases. No cost or quality numbers on the page.
cards.landing: A default routing table for the custom-agent set: locator/analyzer/pattern-finder cheap (FixFlow has the Haiku locator), implementer and reviewer one tier down from the orchestrator. FixFlow runs refuters and verifiers at the orchestrator's tier or higher; this table runs the reviewer on Sonnet.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: HumanLayer does not add an RPI-specific Claude effort setting.
cards.claim: For Claude Code sub-agents the product sets no per-agent effort: the child gets the main session's thinking settings, model:inherit controls the model but not effort, and a direct SDK test found an Opus 5 child ran at medium effort when none was set.
cards.evidence_detail: One 'direct SDK learning test' reported with no sample size.
cards.landing: For L1, whoever sets effort in a Workflow script is the only control; an agent file with model: inherit does not pin effort. Check what effort FixFlow's verifiers actually inherit.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: HumanLayer does not increase the effort.
cards.claim: For Codex sessions every sub-agent uses the parent GPT model; the seven standard children (general-purpose, bash, codebase-analyzer, codebase-locator, codebase-pattern-finder, web-search-researcher, implementer-agent) always run at low effort, and only outline-implementer-agent runs at the parent's effort, so a parent at high gives children low and the outline implementer high.
cards.evidence_detail: Table of eight agents with effort column.
cards.landing: A concrete effort routing: read-only and search children at low, the one agent that does the write work at the parent's effort. Compare with FixFlow verifiers at xhigh.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The outline implementer sub-agent now inherits the parent session's reasoning effort instead of always running at low effort.
cards.claim: Version 0.124.1 (2026-06-26) changed the outline implementer from always-low to the parent's effort, i.e. the write-capable child was moved up while search children stayed low.
cards.evidence_detail: Release note, no reason or numbers given.
cards.landing: Dated evidence that the effort routing was tuned by role after the fact: implementer up, search down.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use the switch when code search speed and cost are more important than Sonnet's added analysis.
cards.claim: An experiments switch drops the three read-only research agents from Sonnet to Haiku while leaving the parent, web researcher, implementers and reviewer unchanged, and both user and organisation settings must allow it.
cards.evidence_detail: Trade-off stated without numbers.
cards.landing: FixFlow's Haiku file locator is the same bet. The switch is evidence that Haiku is used for search only and never for review.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use the shortest path that controls the main risk.
cards.claim: There are four workflows (Oneshot: implement and PR; RPI: questions, research, design discussion, structure outline, implementation, PR; PRD-Oriented: questions, research, PRD, TDD, outline, implementation, PR; Freeform) and the user picks the shortest one that covers the risk of a wrong design.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase table plus the sentence in the explanation page.
cards.landing: FixFlow runs one 40-phase routine for all work. Tiering phases by risk (a small-change path versus a planned path) is a possible change to the ship plan section 0.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: It writes questions about the current system without a review checkpoint.
cards.claim: The first phase turns a ticket into questions about the current codebase with exact source pointers, and the research phase then reads only that question file (skipping ticket.md), so research does not see the intended solution.
cards.evidence_detail: Per-skill 'What it reads' fields: create-research reads exactly one research-questions artifact or a direct query and skips ticket.md unless named.
cards.landing: Matches the 'RPI failed because research returned opinions' fix. For FixFlow, a cold-resume agent could be given questions, not the plan, so it cannot echo the plan back.

cards.source_title: reference/skills-workflows: parallel research, wait for all
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Splits the work and uses parallel research when useful. It waits for every result.
cards.claim: The research skill fans out to parallel sub-agents, waits for all of them, then writes one objective account with code and test references and may run one more pass on open questions.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill behaviour description.
cards.landing: Plain fan-out/join pattern that could be a saved workflow script (W5): split questions, run in parallel, join, one gap pass.

cards.source_title: reference/skills-workflows: design discussion keeps decisions open
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Each decision stays open until you give a clear answer.
cards.claim: The design-discussion skill lists current state, desired state, options and open questions, and may not resolve a question until the user settles it; PRD and TDD skills ask one question per message and need separate approvals (full solution; system design; program design).
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as skill rules.
cards.landing: A mechanical owner-checkpoint rule: agent drafts, user owns the decision. FixFlow's decisions journal could mark each entry 'proposed' or 'settled by owner'.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Each phase names one testable result, the files it changes, and its checks.
cards.claim: The structure outline splits the approved design into vertical slices, each with scope, files, tests, automated checks and manual checks, copied to an overview checklist, and feedback on the outline never starts implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill description plus the explanation page's horizontal-versus-vertical argument.
cards.landing: FixFlow's phases are already slices; the per-phase 'automated checks / manual checks' fields and the overview checklist are template fields the closing message could reuse.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Auto-advanced implementation skips those pauses but still commits after every phase.
cards.claim: Implementation does one phase, runs its checks, reports manual steps, waits for review and commits; auto-advance removes the pause but never the commit, and progress is recorded in the outline itself (phase headings and checked boxes).
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in two places on the page.
cards.landing: Progress lives in the plan file as checkboxes, committed each phase. That makes 'was the routine followed' visible in git history (commit per phase) without a hook.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: plan > structure outline > TDD > PRD > design discussion > research > ticket
cards.claim: When artifacts disagree the later one wins, but for questions about current behaviour the live code beats any document; artifacts are numbered NN-type-slug.md with the next number taken from the highest existing prefix.
cards.evidence_detail: Precedence line and filename tree.
cards.landing: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md already says 'trust it over prose docs'. A written precedence order for plan/register/docs, plus 'live code beats a document about current behaviour', is a short rule that could replace some prose.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Before you switch sessions, write every current decision from this session into the artifact.
cards.claim: Continue in the same session while context remains; before starting a fresh session write every decision into the artifact, then resume with the matching iterate command carrying the feedback in the prompt.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in the guide and the reference.
cards.landing: This is the hand-off rule that makes 'one phase per new session' safe: the cold-resume trial (P1) tests exactly this, so add a close-of-session step 'decisions written to the artifact' to the six-question closing message.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: A fast first draft does not save time when its design is wrong.
cards.claim: Agents write code faster than people review it, so the bottleneck moves to review, and reviewers can change a short document faster than a large PR; hence key choices are put in a short document before code.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument, no numbers; links to his 'Why Software Factories Fail' video.
cards.landing: Rationale for the owner view: a one-page view is the review surface, the PR is not.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Research does not choose a future design.
cards.claim: Research records current behaviour, limits and patterns only, so reviewers can correct facts before they become design assumptions; design then states the desired result and the choices behind it.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument.
cards.landing: FixFlow's register of verified diagnoses is a research artifact in this sense. Keeping 'what exists' separate from 'what to do' gives the refuter a clean fact to check.

cards.source_title: explanation/workflow-phases: system and program design with code-shaped artifacts
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: These examples make internal choices visible before an agent writes the code.
cards.claim: Technical design is reviewed as concrete artifacts (endpoint contracts, tables with their query, call-path diffs, file trees marked NEW/MODIFIED, function signatures), so a missing index or wrong query is found before implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Four worked examples on the page.
cards.landing: A review of a plan as call-path and file-tree diffs is a cheaper reviewer input than reading code. Related to the skipped call-graph tooling decision; he does it by hand in the document.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Auto-advance launches the next RPI session when a completed session reaches `ready_for_input`
cards.claim: A phase handoff is a transition table (flag, source label, destination, skill) driven by effective flags (user override over task default), with a completion check (matching artifact frontmatter type, or next_step_suggestions) and a dedup check so the next session is launched once.
cards.evidence_detail: Design note for the engine, five table rows.
cards.landing: Deterministic control flow instead of the agent deciding to continue. Completion is judged by 'artifact of the right type exists', which is a checkable signal usable for the 'routine was followed' question (W2).

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The task sidebar hides toggles by omitting change handlers, not by disabling switches.
cards.claim: A context shard in the repo is a short per-subsystem markdown note under .agents/context-shards/ listing main components with file paths, a flow diagram, semantics, a gotchas section, and the reasons for historical quirks (for example a persisted field name left unrenamed on purpose). The file does not say how shards are loaded.
cards.evidence_detail: One shard read; its structure is Main Components, Backend Flow, Transition Table, Semantics, UI Visibility, Completion and Dedup, Important Gotchas. Loading rules and the product feature are only in the 0.164.0 release note.
cards.landing: A per-subsystem note with file paths and 'Important Gotchas' is the shape FixFlow could move CLAUDE.md invariants into (jobs lifecycle, outbox, dispatcher), loaded only when that area is touched. Overlaps the knowledge-store design.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Your organization's engineering knowledge compounds across sessions.
cards.claim: Version 0.164.0 (2026-08-25) offers 'Context Shards + Compounding Engineering' in early access, by invitation only; the note gives no mechanism.
cards.evidence_detail: One line; opt-in by contacting HumanLayer.
cards.landing: Evidence the idea is a product bet, not a published method. The mechanism is only inferable from the repo's .agents/context-shards folder.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: launch tasks in separate worktrees, start sessions, check task status and PRs
cards.claim: Version 0.182.0 (2026-10-09) added /hl:orchestrate to break down work, launch tasks in separate worktrees, start sessions, check task status and PRs, and move artifacts between tasks; version 0.183.0 (2026-10-14) added proposed auto-advance defaults per workflow and a workflow chart.
cards.evidence_detail: Two release-note lines.
cards.landing: A saved orchestration skill (one orchestrator, many worktree tasks, one session each) is the workflow-library idea in W4/W5.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: guides an agent through saving your work, setting up a remote host, and starting a new session
cards.claim: A /hl:teleport skill (0.182.0, 2026-10-09) saves the work, sets up another host and starts a new session there on the same task.
cards.evidence_detail: One release-note line; 0.183.0 adds CLI/Claude Code/gh updates on the new host.
cards.landing: A resume-in-a-different-place procedure that depends on the artifacts being complete, the same property P1 tests.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Codex subagents now fork from the caller's context instead of starting cold
cards.claim: Version 0.155.0 (2026-08-12) added automatic context compaction and /compact for Codex, resumable sub-agents after finish or error, and fork-mode Codex sub-agents that start with the caller's context.
cards.evidence_detail: Three release-note lines.
cards.landing: Forking carries the caller's context into a child, the opposite of FixFlow's fresh-context refuters. Both are options; the note says forks are 'dramatic' for delegated work.

cards.source_title: release-notes 0.161.0 (Aug 18, 2026): bounded sub-agent nesting and truncated web results
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: CodeLayer subagents now delegate at most three levels deep
cards.claim: Version 0.161.0 (2026-08-18) caps sub-agent delegation at three levels to stop runaway fork chains, and truncates large web search and fetch results so one lookup cannot crowd out the session.
cards.evidence_detail: Two release-note lines.
cards.landing: Two caps to copy: a depth limit on nested agents and a size limit on tool output returned into context. FixFlow caps outputs already; nesting depth is not stated.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: After `/compact`, earlier messages fold behind one header
cards.claim: Version 0.179.0 (2026-09-29) folds pre-compaction messages behind a header with the kept summary one click away, making visible what compaction kept.
cards.evidence_detail: One release-note line.
cards.landing: Showing the compaction summary is a way to audit what survived. For FixFlow, the closing message in the artifact serves that role across sessions.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: One unreviewed PR at a time keeps the queue honest.
cards.claim: Production recurring agents add a no-op guard (exit if an open PR with the agent's label exists), a concurrency group so a manual run cancels an in-flight scheduled one, a repo markdown memory file included in each prompt, and a '/iterate' comment loop that re-runs the agent on the PR branch with the discussion.
cards.evidence_detail: Described as what the HumanLayer team uses itself, including a scheduled agent that migrates one API procedure per day.
cards.landing: The open-PR guard and the memory file are cheap queue controls; the memory file is the same idea as the knowledge store (update it in a PR so later runs know).

cards.source_title: guide/automation-sessions: ephemeral daemon, permission bypass, shutdown
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: launches the coding agent in the working directory with permission prompts bypassed.
cards.claim: `humanlayer automation run` creates the task, starts a short-lived daemon inside the CI job, runs one session with permission prompts bypassed, streams events to the cloud, and exits with a code reflecting the session result; the session's own prompt tells it to branch, commit, push and open the PR, or the workflow does git afterwards.
cards.evidence_detail: Flags: --ensure-task, --session-name, --metadata-file, --prompt-file, --shutdown-on (inactivity default 2m, or stop), --provider, --model, --coding-agent, --thinking.
cards.landing: The exit code and a metadata file with task and session IDs give a machine-readable record that a session ran, which is the missing signal for 'routine skipped' if FixFlow ever runs phases headless.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: If the user requests an rpi: skill and doesn't mention a file, check here first.
cards.claim: Sessions with a task get an injected block naming the task artifact directory (a symlink), telling the agent to look there first when asked to continue work or run a phase skill with no file named, and forbidding artifact edits through shell tools (python, node, sed), because the UI would miss them.
cards.evidence_detail: Verbatim block, with a Codex variant that says artifacts may only be edited with the apply-patch tool.
cards.landing: A single 'where continuing work lives' pointer injected per session is what a cold-resume agent needs to find the ten frozen facts. The rule 'only edit artifacts with the write tool so edits are observed' is a way to make writes observable (W2).

cards.source_title: explanation/tasks: task-file sync follows tool calls
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: A file does not upload only because another program placed it in the directory.
cards.claim: Task files sync to the cloud only when the agent reads, writes or edits them with its file tools (Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, apply_patch), at .humanlayer/tasks/<slug>/, so the sync record is a by-product of tool calls.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes the mechanism; text artifacts (md, mdx, txt, json, jsonl) up to 10 MB each.
cards.landing: Observation on tool calls is how compliance becomes visible. FixFlow's equivalent would be a hook on file tools, which the review skipped; mark as re-opening hooks.

cards.source_title: explanation/tasks: a task groups sessions with separate phases
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Start a fresh session without losing the task history
cards.claim: A task holds many sessions (research, design, implementation, review), each with its own agent, model, directory, messages and run state, plus shared artifacts and comments that later agents can read, so a fresh session per phase does not lose history.
cards.evidence_detail: Concept page.
cards.landing: Matches 'one phase per new session' with the artifact folder as the memory. Reviewer comments on a plan are read by later agents, which maps to PR review comments in FixFlow.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Set `sourceRef` explicitly to the repository's remote default branch
cards.claim: Workspace config is two JSON files merged over defaults (shared workspace.json, git-ignored workspace.local.json with $patch delete); a worktree starts from origin/main rather than HEAD so default-branch updates do not appear as task changes; copyGlobs copy .env files and .claude/settings.local.json into each worktree; a setupCommand runs after the copy; setupBlocksFirstSession makes the first session wait for setup.
cards.evidence_detail: Field reference with defaults.
cards.landing: FixFlow phases run in worktrees; a worktree that starts from a pinned remote ref and copies the local settings file makes the cold-resume start state reproducible. Check that the settings.local.json copy does not carry permissions into the trial.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Skills and instruction files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) from every repo
cards.claim: In a multi-repo workspace the session is told that CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and skills from every repo are loaded, and for an extra repository the first non-empty of AGENTS.md then CLAUDE.md is injected under a 'Repository Instructions' heading; repo-local settings and MCP config follow the launch directory only.
cards.evidence_detail: Verbatim blocks; also a workspace_setup_status block that tells the agent it may start while setup steps still run and shows failures and stderr.
cards.landing: Instruction files from every repo are concatenated, so any added repo adds to the always-loaded size. Relevant if FixFlow's three runtimes were ever split into repos.

cards.source_title: guide/skills-workflows and reference: worktree timing Now/Later/Never
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Oneshot treats **Later** as **Never**.
cards.claim: Worktree timing is a task-level choice: Now creates the workspace before the first session, Later adds a real create-worktree phase before implementation, Never uses the current checkout; the plan's auto-advance destination changes with it.
cards.evidence_detail: Three-row table plus the auto-advance.md override logic.
cards.landing: Isolation (worktree) is decided at the point implementation starts, after plan review, so research and planning sessions do not each need a worktree.

cards.source_title: reference/skills-workflows: describe-pr and the large-PR walkthrough
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Adds `pr-walkthrough.html` when the PR touches at least 300 lines across at least five files.
cards.claim: The final phase reads the whole diff against the base, checks it against the task artifacts, writes pr-description.md as the PR body, and for PRs of at least 300 lines over at least five files adds an HTML walkthrough with ordered steps, diff excerpts, exclusions and check results.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated thresholds; no data on reviewer effect.
cards.landing: A size-triggered walkthrough with an 'exclusions' section is a possible addition to the owner view. 'Compare diff to plan' is one check an Opus reviewer is already doing.

cards.source_title: guide/codex: per-session provider and effort selection
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Select `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh` reasoning effort.
cards.claim: A session picks provider (claude or codex) and one of four reasoning efforts at launch, and custom Responses endpoints (Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI) are configured by environment variables with HTTPS enforced unless loopback; the Bedrock GPT-5.6 Sol model rejects the reasoning.summary field.
cards.evidence_detail: Setup guide. The 'handoff between Claude Code and Codex' from the inventory is not described here; only release 0.179.0 is cited for it in the inventory.
cards.landing: Effort is a per-session launch parameter in his tool, not a per-agent file setting. A cross-vendor verifier (Codex reviewing Claude work) is an option I did not see argued in these pages.

cards.source_title: guide/codex: environment variables carry no secrets in repo
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Check the installed CLI before you publish a script or runbook.
cards.claim: The docs warn that the launch command can change between CLI releases and tell readers to check `--help` on the installed CLI before writing scripts or runbooks.
cards.evidence_detail: One sentence.
cards.landing: A saved workflow script that shells out to a CLI should record the CLI version it was written against.

cards.source_title: reference/skills-workflows: skill conventions and maintainer note
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: `create-*` commands write a new numbered artifact; `iterate-*` commands edit an existing one in place.
cards.claim: Skills come in create/iterate pairs: create writes a new numbered artifact, iterate edits the existing one in place with its frontmatter intact; 22 skills share one catalog format with six fixed fields (what it does, when to use, what it reads, how it runs, what you get, next step), each skill names its inputs and the ones it must not read, and docs are hand-written and must be checked against the skill registry in the code.
cards.evidence_detail: Catalog structure and the maintainer note at the bottom.
cards.landing: A skill template with 'what it reads / what it must not read / next step' is a ready format for the skills FixFlow is adding. The maintainer note admits prose docs drift from the code registry, the same drift CLAUDE.md warns about.

cards.source_title: reference/skills-workflows: next-step handoff in the final message
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: its final message names the next command
cards.claim: Each skill ends by naming the next command, auto-advance never creates a duplicate newer phase, each transition turns itself off after it runs, and design-to-outline, PRD-to-TDD, TDD-to-outline and outline-to-implementation never auto-advance (the human checkpoints).
cards.evidence_detail: Stated rules and a five-row transition table.
cards.landing: The 'next command' line in a closing message is a cheap, checkable handoff field. Self-disabling auto-advance is a guard against loops.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use `bun` for everything, never npm, pnpm, or yarn.
cards.claim: One package manager for everything and dependencies added to the package that needs them, never the root; the root also pins engines (node >=24) and packageManager so agents do not pick another tool.
cards.evidence_detail: One CONTRIBUTING line plus package.json engines/packageManager fields.
cards.landing: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md already lists commands per runtime; pinning tools in package metadata moves a line out of prose.

gaps: scripts/run-silent.ts, scripts/hook-prepush.ts, scripts/hooks/pre-push, scripts/check-sentry-closures.ts and the anti-slop oxlint rule files are not in my file list, so what the silent runner actually prints on failure, what the hooks do, and how the hooks are bound to Claude Code events (settings.json) are unread.

The context-shards folder gave me only auto-advance.md. How shards are selected and loaded into a session is not in these files; the only product statement is the one-line 0.164.0 release note (no mechanism).

release-notes.md was keyword-scanned (shard, orchestrate, verif, compact, fork, effort, backpressure, silent, hook), not read in full; no hit mentions verifiers or backpressure, so those topics have no card from this bundle.
The Codex handoff (session handoff between Claude Code and Codex, release 0.179.0 in the inventory) is not described in guide/codex.md; that page covers setup only.

The docs have no measured numbers on effort or model routing; the sub-agent routing is a configuration table with no cost or quality data, so nothing here supports or refutes the SlopCodeBench 'medium matches xhigh' claim.
The docs pages are unsigned and undated, so source_date is '2026-11' (approximate) except where a release-note version gives a date.
